gaps.topic: Loader: measured first-visit timeline, valid milestones, Core Web Vitals
gaps.question: In a scratch build (not src/) with the inline loader of at most 2 KB from ready-check §15 A0, the lazy Stage chunk on the pinned stack (React 19.3.1, fiber 9.8.2, drei 10.7.9, three 0.187.0, postprocessing 6.39.6, core shaders from webgl-magic §3–5) and the preloaded Literata caps subset (type-sound-legal §A.7), measure cold and warm on Lighthouse mobile (Moto G Power, Slow 4G, 4x CPU) and on desktop: (a) the loader's first paint; (b) document.fonts.load('700 1em Display'); (c) Stage chunk fetch and evaluation; (d) gl.compileAsync, with and without KHR_parallel_shader_compile; (e) the first advance(). Then record the LCP element and time, CLS and INP under each candidate policy: ready-check (minimum 1,600 ms plus a reveal of about 1,100 ms, 6 s per milestone); shell-lobby §10 (show only above 400 ms, minimum 900 ms, cap 3 s); webgl-magic §6.3 (cap 1,500 ms). Check against web.dev's LCP rules whether a hero h1 painted under an opaque overlay, or SplitText characters at opacity 0, can become the LCP element. Output: the milestone list with per-milestone timeouts, the minimum show time, the skip threshold, the cap, and exit timings that keep LCP at or below 2,500 ms (stack-modernization §10.4).
gaps.why_it_matters: Four reports set conflicting loader parameters (see the loader contradiction), and two of the proposed gates can never resolve in this build. ready-check's 'textures' gate waits for drei useProgress '!active && progress === 100'. In drei 10.7.9 (core/Progress.js, checked in scratchpad deps19), useProgress starts at progress 0 and changes only when THREE.DefaultLoadingManager fires, and no loader runs in the procedural scene. So that gate always times out at 6 s, and every first visit would last at least 6 s with a grey segment. shell-lobby's 'audio' and 'data' pips have nothing to load either. Without measured numbers, owner idea #1 cannot be specified, and a first-visit minimum of about 2.7 s risks the LCP budget.

gaps.topic: One tone-mapping operator for the shared canvas (HDR core + brand-colour logos)
gaps.question: Use the webgl-magic bench (scratchpad entries/bench.jsx): one fixed Canvas, one EffectComposer with Bloom (mipmapBlur, threshold 1), then Vignette, then ToneMapping last, multisampling 0. Render the hextech core together with enamel-and-gold logos (Qt #41CD52, TypeScript #3178C6, Supabase #3FCF8E, Spring Boot #6DB33F; gold sides #C89B3C; materials from 3d-logos §3.7). Compare three set-ups: (a) NEUTRAL for everything, with the core's uIntensity, vein multiplier, halo multiplier and Bloom luminanceThreshold re-tuned until the core matches webgl-magic §3; (b) AgX for everything, with the logo colours pre-compensated; (c) switching the ToneMapping mode while #stack is active. For (c), find whether ToneMappingEffect.mode in postprocessing 6.39.6 is a define, which forces an EffectPass recompile (measure the hitch in ms), or a uniform. Make the LOW tier, which has no composer and uses renderer.toneMapping, match the chosen result. Output: the chosen operator, the final HDR constants and side-by-side screenshots.
gaps.why_it_matters: webgl-magic (§0.6, §2.2, §5.2) tuned the core for AgX. 3d-logos (§0.5, §3.7) ran an A/B: AgX greyed Qt, TypeScript, Supabase and Redis and turned the gold beige, so that report requires NEUTRAL. webgl-magic §2 puts the core and the logos on one canvas with one composer, so only one operator can apply at a time. This blocks the look of both the hero and the Stack section.

gaps.topic: Gold-frame section reveal (brief: every section in gold frames, revealed by GSAP on scroll)
gaps.question: Specify one reusable entrance for a framed section: a 2 px gradient border, 4 px ornament strips sitting 6 px outside it (shell-lobby §9.1), a title, body text and children. (1) Extract the client's own intro and outro keyframes for framed surfaces from raw.communitydragon.org/latest/plugins/rcp-fe-lol-uikit and rcp-fe-common-libs (dialog frame, flyout frame, sub-border, content blocks): durations, easings, order and transform-origin. (2) Prototype at least three ways to draw on a 2 px gradient border: an SVG rect overlay with DrawSVG or stroke-dashoffset; a CSS mask or clip-path wipe; a conic mask animated through @property. Measure paint and composite cost with 4 to 6 framed sections on screen over the animating fixed WebGL canvas, in Chromium, Firefox and Playwright WebKit. Output: timeline in ms, easing tokens, stagger, ScrollTrigger start and end, play-once versus replay, content visible by default without JS, and a reduced-motion variant.
gaps.why_it_matters: Only static frame CSS exists (lol-client-ui frame, shell-lobby .hx-dialog, stack-modernization @utility hx-frame). None of the nine reports defines how a section enters, yet it is the most repeated motion on the page. Border-image and padding-box gradient borders cannot be stroke-animated as written. codebase-audit B2 shows today's site leaves content at opacity 0 when rAF does not tick, so the reveal must be progressive enhancement.

gaps.topic: Adaptive quality on real devices: tier sampling under gated rendering, plus mobile and Safari capabilities
gaps.question: (1) webgl-magic §2.2 renders with frameloop 'never' and calls advance() only while stage.active or stage.dirty. drei 10.7.9 PerformanceMonitor samples performance.now() only inside useFrame, and clears its frame buffer only after a window of at least 250 ms. So a pause (scrolling away, a hidden tab) or on-demand idle renders of the champion logo should produce windows near 0 fps, which trigger onDecline; with flipflops 3, onFallback then pins LOW. Confirm this in a test, then specify a fix: reset frames on resume, sample only during continuous rendering, or a small custom monitor. (2) Set explicit bounds for 60, 120 and 144 Hz displays. (3) From web3dsurvey.com or similar fleet data, find what share of iOS Safari 18/26, Android Chrome and macOS Safari WebGL2 clients expose EXT_color_buffer_half_float or EXT_color_buffer_float, KHR_parallel_shader_compile, and an unmasked WEBGL_debug_renderer_info. Also check whether iOS Low Power Mode caps rAF at 30 fps. Output: starting-tier rules per platform, a fallback when only 8-bit buffers are available, and corrected allowHigh() logic.
gaps.why_it_matters: Every GPU number comes from one Intel UHD iGPU in an embedded Chromium (webgl-magic §8, §11). webgl-magic §7.2 says the default bounds are 50–60 fps, but the drei 10.7.9 source sets 'refreshrate > 100 ? [60,100] : [40,60]'. A monitor that misreads paused rendering would silently drop every visitor to LOW, the opposite of premium. Without half-float buffers, the selective bloom at threshold 1 stops working (webgl-magic §5.2), and whether iPhones expose those buffers is UNVERIFIED.

gaps.topic: Champion Select inside a Lenis-smoothed scrolling page
gaps.question: Prototype the Stack section in scratch with Lenis 1.3.27 (autoRaf off, driven by gsap.ticker as in webgl-magic §2.3), ScrollTrigger and the fixed canvas. (1) champ-select §6.5 starts an intro of about 6.2 s when the section is 40% in view, and skips it on any pointer, key or scroll event. How long after the last wheel or touch input does Lenis keep emitting scroll events at the default lerp of .1, and does that skip the intro immediately? Define start and skip rules, for example start once velocity stays under X for Y ms, and skip only when the visitor scrolls away. (2) Should the section be pinned? Give its height at 1440x900, 1280x720, 768x1024 and 375x812. (3) After LOCK IN the grid collapses and the build sheet grows: measure the CLS, the cost of ScrollTrigger.refresh() and the effect on triggers further down the page. (4) Measure the drift in px between the DOM splash box and the 3D logo with the rect cache (webgl-magic §2.5) during Lenis scrolling at 60 and 120 Hz. (5) Check that the #stack/<id> hash (champ-select §5.2) works with Lenis anchors:true and the header scroll-spy.
gaps.why_it_matters: champ-select specifies a 1280x720 app screen, and webgl-magic a DOM-synced logo on a fixed canvas. Nobody has tested either inside a scrolling page. As written, the skip rule will probably cancel the signature lock-in intro (owner idea #2) for anyone who scrolls into the section. The build-sheet expansion is a likely CLS source.

gaps.topic: Project detail / case-study view and full project grid (screen nobody covered)
gaps.question: Which client screen should the project detail view follow, and what are its measurements? Read these live client plugins on CommunityDragon (raw.communitydragon.org/latest/plugins/<name>/global/default/, CSS, JS and trans.json): rcp-fe-lol-champion-details, rcp-fe-lol-collections, rcp-fe-lol-store and rcp-fe-lol-match-history. Extract (1) the champion detail and skin-viewing modal: layout boxes at 1280x720, gallery or carousel behaviour, open and close motion (ms, easing), close and back controls; (2) the Collection grid: tile size, gutters, filters and sort, for the 'ALL (11)' grid under the lobby banners (shell-lobby §5.2). Map both to a case-study modal or panel at 1280, 768 and 375 px with 16:10 screenshots. Include a deep-link scheme that works with Lenis anchors (#projects/<slug> alongside #stack/<id>), where focus goes on open and returns on close, and the data fields the view needs.
gaps.why_it_matters: shell-lobby §5.2 gives every banner a 'Details' button, and the champ-select §5.2 build-sheet carousel shows projects 'with screenshot and link', but no report says where either leads. codebase-audit §10 deferred the detail dialog to a later lot with no spec, and §4.1 shows the case-study fields don't exist yet. Recruiters read this screen first, and it is the only screen we plan that has no measurements.

gaps.topic: Cost of the DOM effects layered over a live WebGL canvas
gaps.question: With the fixed canvas rendering every tick (the hero state), measure frame time and dropped frames in Chromium, Firefox and Playwright WebKit on Windows, at full speed and with 4x CPU throttling, for: the sticky header's backdrop-filter: blur(12px) over the canvas (shell-lobby §3.1, §3.7); the PLAY hover swirl, made of feTurbulence noise inside two masks whose dash offset animates, drawn twice with blur(2px) and blur(4px) (shell-lobby §3.4); the rotating conic LOCK IN border (one turn per 15 s); the ready-check title's infinite 1,500 ms text-shadow pulse; a full-stage mix-blend-mode: screen flash; gradient-border frames while scrolling. For each effect, decide whether it must be pre-rendered (for example, the swirl noise baked into a small image we draw ourselves), limited to (hover: hover), or dropped below a given tier. Output: a table of costs in ms and a downgrade matrix by tier and engine.
gaps.why_it_matters: webgl-magic §7.2 keeps the GPU at 8 ms or less 'so DOM compositing has headroom', but no report measured the DOM side. backdrop-filter over an animating canvas re-blurs every frame, and SVG filters are often rasterised on the CPU. The header and hero carry the most of these effects at once, and they are the first things on screen.

gaps.question: List every original glyph and ornament the reports require, with its sizes and states: nav active pointer (15 px); top and bottom frame strips; banner trim, rod and crest rings; level pill and XP ring; PLAY crest monogram (56 px); header and LOCK IN linework brackets; grid reticle (81x81); five 34x34 lane glyphs; ban glyph; contact-dialog icon; toast medallion ticks; mastery crests; challenge tokens; footer icons. For each one, view the CommunityDragon sprite without downloading or tracing it, and describe the client's shape grammar: stroke weights, gem shapes, taper angles, gradient stops. Then write construction rules for our own SVGs: grid, stroke widths at 1x and 2x, gold gradient stops, and the two-tone rule (#C8AA6E, with #785A28 at 50%). Finally, check whether game-icons.net (CC BY 3.0), Tabler (MIT), Phosphor (MIT) or Lucide (ISC) cover the lane and role glyphs.
gaps.why_it_matters: shell-lobby §13 says the nav pointer, frame strips and banner art were never seen, and it ships 1 px hairline placeholders in their place. champ-select §5.1 needs 5 new glyphs, and codebase-audit §9 says the current 'L' crest echoes the League logo and must be replaced. Most of the client's premium feel comes from this ornament layer, and none of it can be copied. Without construction rules, each component's ornaments will be drawn ad hoc.

gaps.topic: Legal limits on copying the client GUI, and on 3D versions of framework marks
gaps.question: (1) Beyond Riot's Legal Jibber Jabber policy and US trademark law (already covered), does reproducing the client's look carry copyright or trade-dress risk under EU, French, Tunisian and US law? The owner's country is UNVERIFIED; ask. Assess each of these: the exact PLAY arrow outline from the uikit JS (concave arc r 21.461, 8.4 px deep; shell-lobby §3.2); the LOCK IN clip-path polygon (champ-select §3.5); the 215/840/225 header grid; timing and easing values read from Riot's CSS; client strings such as 'MATCH FOUND' and 'WAITING FOR OTHER PLAYERS'; a blue hexagonal crystal in gold rings that evokes Arcane's Hextech gem. Starting points to verify: CJEU C-393/09 (BSA: a GUI can be protected by copyright), C-406/10 (SAS Institute), Lotus v. Borland, Apple v. Microsoft. (2) Do gold-bevelled 3D renderings of the Python, Flutter, TypeScript and Angular logos break those brands' rules: the PSF's 'ask first' for derived versions, 'don't alter' for Flutter and TypeScript, and the credit required by Angular's CC BY 4.0? Output: each element classed as safe, alter (and how) or avoid. Not legal advice.
gaps.why_it_matters: type-sound-legal §C.3 says pixel-faithful copies of client artwork, SVG ornament paths included, would make the site a derivative work. Yet shell-lobby and champ-select prescribe the client's exact geometry, and the owner wants the site to feel like the real client. 3d-logos §2.1 and §10 leave the derived-logo question UNVERIFIED. These answers decide how literal the build can be, so they are needed before components are drawn.

gaps.question: For each of the 11 entries in src/data/projects.ts, check whether the links resolve and which front-end stack the live site actually runs: Next.js (/_next/ and __NEXT_DATA__), Create React App (static/js/main.*), Angular (ng-version), Vite or Lovable, plus hosting headers. Capture 16:10 screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 with Playwright into the scratchpad, as internal evidence only; publishing the client site sammedicale.com.tn needs permission. Then choose an image pipeline that works on Vite 8.3.7 with Rolldown: check vite-imagetools' peer range against a sharp prebuild script, and report AVIF and WebP sizes in bytes at banner, card and case-study sizes. Output: a table of claimed versus detected stacks, corrected 'games played' counts per framework, and screenshot paths for the owner to confirm.
gaps.why_it_matters: champ-select §5.1–5.2 derives the lane mains and 'games played' (Spring Boot 6, Next.js 5, PostgreSQL 4…) from projects.ts. codebase-audit §4.1 flags PlanIfy (page title 'React App' while it claims Next.js + React Native), MONO (hosted on Lovable while it claims Spring Boot + Next.js), two example.com links and one bookbub.com link. No screenshots exist for the banners, the build-sheet carousel or case studies, and no report chose an image tool for Vite 8.

contradictions.between: ready-check §15/§18 vs shell-lobby §10 vs webgl-magic §6.3 vs type-sound-legal §A.7.5 (the loader, owner idea #1)
contradictions.issue:
The reports disagree on every loader parameter.
- Sequence. ready-check starts at MATCH ACCEPTED / WAITING FOR OTHER PLAYERS. shell-lobby shows MATCH FOUND, auto-presses ACCEPT at 300 ms and ends on 'MATCH ACCEPTED', although the client shows that title at accept time (ready-check §0.2).
- Milestones. ready-check: you, fonts, core compile, useProgress textures, window load. shell-lobby: fonts, hero scene, textures, data, audio. webgl-magic: DOM interactive, fonts, Stage import, compileAsync, first advance.
- Caps. ready-check: 6 s per milestone, a 10 s CSS failsafe, 'STILL WAITING' at 8 s and 'ENTER ANYWAY' at 12 s. Those last two states are unreachable, because every gate settles by about 6 s. shell-lobby: 3 s. webgl-magic and type-sound-legal: 1.5 s.
- Minimum show time. ready-check: 1,600 ms on a first visit, 500 ms returning. shell-lobby: 900 ms.
- Skip threshold. ready-check: under 300 ms. shell-lobby: under 400 ms.
- Exit. ready-check: the ring bursts and FLIPs into the hero core, then the header slides in. shell-lobby: letterbox bars retract over 400 ms. webgl-magic: camera dolly from z 8.5 to 5.2 over 1.6 s, with a flash at 0.9 s.
- 3D chunk. shell-lobby puts PLAY into 'patching' instead of blocking; the other two wait for the 3D.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Write one loader spec sized from Gap 1's measurements: text sequence, milestones, timeouts, minimum show time, skip rules, and one master intro timeline that merges ready-check A3/A4 with webgl-magic's playIntro. Drop the 'textures', 'audio' and 'data' gates, which can never resolve.

contradictions.between: champ-select (§0, §5.5 'Versions') and 3d-logos §4.4 vs webgl-magic §0.1/§1, stack-modernization §0.3/§1/§6 and threejs-skill (Decision)
contradictions.issue: champ-select says to keep @react-three/fiber 8.18.0 and drei 9.122.0 on React 18.3, and 3d-logos' LogoChampion component is written against only fiber 8.18 / drei 9.122 APIs. The other three reports pin React 19.3.1, fiber 9.8.2, drei 10.7.9 and three 0.187.0, plus @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.2, which cannot install on fiber 8. webgl-magic and stack-modernization both built and rendered that React 19 set.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Adopt the React 19 set with exact pins (react must stay below 19.4, three below 0.188), and remove champ-select's React 18 pins. Re-test LogoChampion on fiber 9.8.2 under StrictMode, which now also double-invokes inside Canvas, using the 'never' frame-loop driver.

contradictions.between: webgl-magic §0.6, §2.2 (Canvas gl.toneMapping = AgX), §5.2 (<ToneMapping mode=AGX/> last) vs 3d-logos §0.5, §3.7, §8
contradictions.issue: webgl-magic applies AgX to the whole stage to suit the HDR core. 3d-logos measured AgX desaturating brand colours and turning gold beige, and requires NEUTRAL wherever logos render. Both render on the single shared canvas and composer of webgl-magic §2, which applies one operator.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Choose one operator, or a per-section switch whose cost has been measured, and re-tune the core's HDR constants (Gap 2).

contradictions.between: ready-check §16 Storyboard B vs shell-lobby §3.3, §4.3, §7.5, §11 vs the approved mockup's 'Contact · Match found' cell
contradictions.issue:
The contact flow differs on four points.
- Trigger. ready-check: the form's SEND button. shell-lobby: releasing the header PLAY button 'opens the Match found contact modal', while the contact section is a social panel plus the form in a dialog frame.
- Queue timer. ready-check: a 240x64 card under the header profile ring. shell-lobby: the PLAY label reads 'IN QUEUE 0:03'.
- After sending. ready-check: a MATCH FOUND dialog with an 8 s countdown that pauses on hover; the visitor must click ACCEPT for a message that is already sent (a timeout path auto-completes), then a persistent toast. shell-lobby: a small post-game (VICTORY gradient line, a meter filling over 900 ms, then a celebration toast).
- Mockup. The ring shows a numeral '8' (ready-check §0.1: the client has none), with the line 'Abdelmatine wants to work with you'.
contradictions.resolution_needed: One storyboard, signed off by the owner. It must settle: section or modal, where the queue timer lives, whether ACCEPT is a required click, which success screen to show, and what the header PLAY button does.

contradictions.between: shell-lobby §0 and §1 (corrections 1–2), §3.2, §3.5 vs the brief, the approved mockup (.play-hex, .nav .on:after) and codebase-audit §10 (ClientHeader 'serif-caps tabs with the fading gold underline')
contradictions.issue: The brief and mockup ask for a hexagonal PLAY button with teal text and main tabs with a fading gold underline. shell-lobby measured the live client instead. PLAY is a 162x58 arrow plate whose concave left edge hugs a round crest, with a #F0E6D2 label. The active main tab has a 15 px pointer at the top edge and a glow rising from the bottom. The fading underline belongs only to the secondary tabs (12 px, weight 500, .1em).
contradictions.resolution_needed: The owner chooses client accuracy (arrow plate, pointer and glow), the approved mockup (hexagon, underline), or a deliberate mix. Record the choice in the design spec.

contradictions.between: lol-client-ui (Typography), champ-select §1, ready-check §16 B1 and the approved mockup (Marcellus SC + Barlow from Google Fonts) vs type-sound-legal §0 and §A
contradictions.issue: For display text, the reports propose Marcellus SC or Cinzel against Literata 600–700. For body text, Barlow against Source Sans 3 Variable. The Literata option is a self-hosted 21.6 KB subset with capitals only and no italics. type-sound-legal measured Marcellus' figures as unusable for counters and timers (hanging, proportional, no tabular numerals) and Cinzel's contrast at about 2.3x Beaufort's. champ-select's type table also has italic rows: the others'-turn header at 22/20 and the skin name at 18/22, weight 500. The caps-only upright subset cannot render those.
contradictions.resolution_needed: The owner approves Literata and Source Sans 3 after an A/B in the hi-fi mockups. Move the italic and mixed-case roles to the body face's italic, or widen the subset and budget the extra bytes.

contradictions.between: approved mockup (4 tabs: HOME, PROJECTS, STACK, CONTACT; counters '12 PROJECTS · 5 YEARS') vs shell-lobby §3.7, §4.3, §11 (5 tabs with CAREER; icon tabs for Profile, Collection and Loot (CV); About, Career and Stats sections; a chat dock) vs codebase-audit §10, §12 (delete ChatBox; the about, experience, education, CV, testimonial and counter content does not exist) and champ-select §5.4 (chat skipped)
contradictions.issue: The reports disagree on the section list, the nav labels and whether there is a chat dock, and three of shell-lobby's sections have no content. The '12 projects' counter also conflicts with projects.ts, which has 11 entries: 2 are example.com placeholders and 1 is a third-party link.
contradictions.resolution_needed: The owner fixes the v1 information architecture, a fallback for missing content (for example, fold Stats into About and hide Career until content exists), whether a chat dock exists, and what each counter means.

contradictions.between: champ-select §5.5 vs webgl-magic §9 vs 3d-logos §0, §3–5, §8 (3D logo build, material, lighting, shadow)
contradictions.issue:
The three reports specify the 3D logos differently.
- Geometry. champ-select: depth .18–.24 world units, outward bevel .03/.02, curveSegments 12 (8 above 10 kB), scale.y = -1. webgl-magic: depth 2.4 SVG units, outward bevel .45/.27, rotateX(π) baked in. 3d-logos: clean the paths, inward bevel with bevelOffset = -size from a per-logo table, depth 2, toCreasedNormals before scaling, mergeGroups, mesh scale [k,-k,k].
- Material. champ-select: brand-colour face with metalness .3, roughness .35, clearcoat 1. 3d-logos: enamel face (roughness .38, metalness .05, clearcoat .6, flatShading) with gold #C89B3C sides. webgl-magic: all-gold #C8AA6E with a brand-colour fresnel halo.
- Environment. champ-select: drei Environment at resolution 64 with Lightformers. webgl-magic: resolution 256. 3d-logos: RoomEnvironment through PMREM, set per material on the logos only.
- Shadow. champ-select: ContactShadows. 3d-logos: avoid it, since it re-renders the whole shared scene every frame; use a blob shadow.
- Path source. webgl-magic imports the simple-icons npm package. 3d-logos and stack-modernization copy the paths into src/data, with the Angular CC BY 4.0 and Duke BSD notices.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Adopt the 3d-logos pipeline: it is the only one rendered for all 20 logos, and its §8 corrects the other two. The owner chooses between enamel-and-gold and webgl-magic's all-gold body with a brand halo. Write one lighting and shadow spec for the shared stage.

contradictions.between: champ-select §5.5 vs webgl-magic §9 vs 3d-logos §0.1, §4.2, §5.1 (React, React Native, C and C++ logos)
contradictions.issue: React has three incompatible builds. champ-select uses three TubeGeometry ellipses (rx 11, ry 4.2) plus a sphere of radius 2.05, and warns that a non-uniformly scaled TorusGeometry distorts the tube. webgl-magic uses exactly that: TorusGeometry(1, .055, 12, 128) scaled (1, .36, 1). 3d-logos extrudes the Simple Icons react outline, shared with React Native plus our phone ring. For C and C++, champ-select builds a hexagonal prism with raised letters, while the Simple Icons c mark is only a bold C and cplusplus is a single shape.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Apply the owner's rule that 3D shapes must match the real logo. Either use the exact extruded outline everywhere, or build a true 3D React atom from TubeGeometry, never a scaled torus. Decide whether C and C++ use the hexagon mark (gilbarbara relief) or the letter-only marks.

contradictions.between: webgl-magic §2 (frameloop 'never', gsap.ticker → lenis.raf → advance; invalidate() does nothing; DPR from pixel budgets of 2.4/1.2/0.6 MP) vs champ-select §5.5, §6.6, 3d-logos §4.4 and threejs-skill §9.2, §9.4
contradictions.issue:
The reports describe three frame-loop models and two DPR policies for the same single canvas.
- champ-select: frameloop 'demand' with invalidate() from GSAP's onUpdate, dpr [1, 1.75] ([1, 1.5] on mobile), and in reduced motion 'static logo, drag to rotate only'.
- 3d-logos §4.4 also says to call invalidate() under 'demand'.
- threejs-skill: frameloop 'always', dpr capped at [1, 2].
Drag-to-rotate cannot work on webgl-magic's canvas, which has pointer-events: none and uses #root as its event source. codebase-audit B16 also warns that OrbitControls-style handlers set touch-action: none, which traps touch scrolling.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Make webgl-magic's driver and pixel budgets canonical, and delete the demand/invalidate advice. In reduced motion, show either a single still frame or a drag handler scoped to the DOM that keeps touch scrolling.

contradictions.between: champ-select §5.1–5.2 vs 3d-logos §0.1, §1, §4.2 vs webgl-magic §9 vs codebase-audit §4.2
contradictions.issue:
The reports disagree on how many champions there are, what the 3D build costs and how the 2D tiles look.
- champ-select: all 20 SVGs in public/icons 'qualify'; 20 tiles plus a random tile; the mains include Next.js (MID) and PostgreSQL (JUNGLE).
- 3d-logos: 14 of the 20 files must be replaced. LOGOS3D covers 11 logos, without Next.js, PostgreSQL, NestJS, Node, Redis, Supabase or MinIO. NestJS needs a worker (68 ms build) and PostgreSQL needs QA at 2x. The 154 ms and 4.7 MB budget covers those 11 only.
- webgl-magic: grid tiles are monochrome inline Simple Icons paths using currentColor.
- codebase-audit: stacks.ts lists 12 technologies, 5 of which no project uses.
contradictions.resolution_needed: The owner fixes the final champion list and the 'mains'. Extend LOGOS3D to every listed technology, including PostgreSQL and Next.js, and re-budget the build. Pick one 2D tile style (brand colour or monochrome gold), sourced from Simple Icons paths.

contradictions.between: type-sound-legal §C.3–C.4 vs the approved mockup, shell-lobby §3.2, §7.4–7.5, §8.3, champ-select §3.5 and the current header (codebase-audit)
contradictions.issue:
type-sound-legal bans Riot nouns in UI copy (Summoner, Honor, RP/LP, Clash and others), and says pixel-faithful client artwork or SVG ornament paths make the site a derivative work. The other material breaks both rules.
- Copy. The mockup's form label is 'Summoner name'. shell-lobby proposes 'honor ceremony' testimonial cards, an 'Honor: testimonials count' emblem and an 'LP-style card'. The current header shows RP/LP counters.
- Geometry. shell-lobby rebuilds the PLAY path from the uikit arrow outline (arc r 21.46, 8.4 px deep). champ-select gives the LOCK IN clip-path polygon exactly as it appears in the client CSS.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Review all UI copy against the naming rule. Decide whether measured outlines may ship as they are or must be altered (Gap 9).

contradictions.between: champ-select §4 vs ready-check §14, §18 vs shell-lobby §2 vs stack-modernization §3.3 (@theme)
contradictions.issue:
The same names point to different curves.
- champ-select: cs.slam = 1,0,1,1; cs.settle = 0,0,0,1.
- ready-check: rc-slam = .2,.9,0,1; rc-mag = 1,0,1,1.
- shell-lobby: settle = .2,.9,0,1; sharp-out = 0,0,0,1; snap-in = 1,0,1,1; pop = 0,1,1,1.
- stack-modernization: --ease-hx-settle = 0,0,.33,1; --ease-hx-slam = 1,0,1,1.
'settle' names three different curves and 'slam' two. Tailwind tokens and GSAP CustomEase ids taken from different reports will silently diverge.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Keep one easing table (id, cubic-bezier, uses) that feeds both @theme and CustomEase.create, with names nobody else uses. For example: snap 1,0,1,1; settle 0,0,0,1; show .2,.9,0,1; glow 0,0,.33,1; plus champ-select's specialised curves.

contradictions.between: lol-client-ui (toasts slide in from the right) and ready-check §16 B3, §17 vs shell-lobby §9.2 vs stack-modernization §4.2
contradictions.issue: ready-check slides the toast in (x 24 → 0) and keeps it until the user closes it, so that the auto-closing countdown still meets WCAG 2.2.1. shell-lobby uses a 422x135 celebration toast that grows vertically (scaleY .5 → 1 over 500 ms), sits bottom-right and dismisses itself after 5 s. stack-modernization makes it a single role=status live region.
contradictions.resolution_needed: One toast spec covering entrance (shell-lobby's correction applies), how long it stays (persistent for the contact result), size, stacking and position.

contradictions.between: ready-check §19 vs champ-select §5.1 vs codebase-audit §10 (useSfx with 'original clips') vs type-sound-legal §B
contradictions.issue:
The reports disagree on recorded clips versus synthesis, and on the cue list and recipes.
- ready-check: WebAudio cues. Match found is two partials (1318 and 1976 Hz) with a 1.2 s decay over a 300 ms noise swell. Also an accept click and chime, pentatonic ticks C5–A5 as loader segments fill, and a 'ready' arpeggio.
- champ-select: own recorded clips, 4 at most (hover tick, lock chime, phase stinger, slash).
- type-sound-legal: everything synthesized, no files. Cues are hover, click, matchFound (a 4.66 s Risset bell), lockIn and hum. Sound is off by default and the AudioContext starts only after a click or keydown.
Loader cues can never be heard on a first visit: no gesture has happened yet and sound starts off.
contradictions.resolution_needed: One cue list with recipes and triggers. Drop the loader cues or accept that they stay silent. If champ-select's phase stinger and slash stay, add them to the synth module.

contradictions.issue: type-sound-legal adds a 'max-age=31536000, immutable' rule for /assets/(.*). stack-modernization shows that unhashed files from public/assets (such as foto.jpg) are also served under /assets/, so that rule would freeze them for a year. Its fix is to move Vite's hashed output with build.assetsDir '_app'.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Make only /_app/(.*) and versioned /fonts/*-vN.woff2 files immutable. Never ship the /assets/(.*) rule.

contradictions.between: approved mockup (.banner-card 150x260, V-tail at 88%) vs shell-lobby §5.1–5.2 (196x592, aspect .331, width clamp(168px, 15.3vw, 216px), a 420 px mobile variant)
contradictions.issue: The banner aspect ratios differ by about 1.75x. At the client's proportions, the five-banner row alone is about 510–650 px tall. shell-lobby fills each banner with a crest, a year pill, the name, 3 metric tokens, 2 framework diamonds and hover buttons, but codebase-audit §4.1 shows no project metrics exist yet.
contradictions.resolution_needed: Choose the banner aspect and how much content it holds at each breakpoint, based on the project data that actually exists.
